solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: African nation importing fifth of sugar beet

indicators.note: a country importing goods brings them inside its borders, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Chad is a landlocked country in central Africa

indicators.note: asks for only the letter in position five of the following word

parts.note: the fifth letter of sugar

explanation.surface: A country in Africa brings in some of its sugar from beet crops.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes inside CHAD, after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy variety of the beet plant, grown for its leaves and stalks rather than its root.

clue.text: Spooner's contemptible chef collected records

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: base means contemptible, a cook is a chef; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: A despised chef has had his records gathered together.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the B and C sounds of the two words gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A casebook is a file where a doctor or detective keeps records of cases, collected in one volume.

clue.text: Vibrant diamante pants

indicators.note: British slang pants means rubbish or badly done, so the letters are a mess to be reordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Trousers covered in sparkly sequins are lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish or badly done, so it signals a jumble; it looks like the trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means full of life and energy, a synonym of vibrant.

clue.text: The exact thing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: grammatical term for the word 'the'
second meaning: read literally, a precise item

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase meaning the genuine article; split it, and the first word is defined by its own grammatical name.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the word 'the' is called this; and 'definite' means exact while 'article' means thing.

clue.text: Rash little rascal with naughty books

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
rude in the sense of risqué
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A cheeky child is reckless enough to look at saucy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe acting without proper thought for the consequences; they are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: The same doctor briefly turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards
made brief, so the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: The same physician appeared again, only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDIC loses its last letter, then reads upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin for the same, used in citations to refer back to an author already mentioned.

clue.text: Attack with gun whilst I pop out

indicators.note: out in the sense of out of place or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is assaulted by a gunman while the speaker has nipped out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pistol-whip is to beat someone using a handgun as a club, an attack made with a gun.

clue.text: Dispassionate representation of Monteverdi's aunt

indicators.note: a representation renders something in a new form, so the letters are presented in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A cool, detached portrait of the composer Monteverdi's aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undemonstrative does not show feelings openly, which matches being unemotional or dispassionate.

clue.text: Inventive American journalist beginning to interview boy

parts.note: ED is short for editor

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word, meaning just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of interview
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A creative American reporter starts interviewing a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inventive' looks like a mere adjective but marks an inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Regularly treat one unspecified condition

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of treat
any means one, whichever

explanation.surface: A doctor routinely treats some unnamed ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetany is a medical condition of involuntary muscle spasms, often from low calcium.

clue.text: Difficulty moving head after small contretemps

indicators.note: says the word before it is placed later in the answer than the words that follow it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tiff is a minor quarrel
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a stiff neck after a minor row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' sounds anatomical, matching 'difficulty moving', but it is a headland; it is placed after the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffness is the condition of joints or muscles that resist bending, a direct noun synonym.

clue.text: Daughters break bank

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter(s) in genealogies
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: Children smash open a savings bank, or break into one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money, but here it is a bank of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift is a heap of snow or sand piled by the wind, which is a bank in the sense of a mound.

clue.text: Boyfriend with case of non-vintage wine

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell, so only the outside letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of non-vintage

explanation.surface: A boyfriend turns up with a box of cheap, non-vintage wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a box of bottles but asks for the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaune is a red Burgundy wine named after the town in the Côte d'Or where it is produced.

clue.text: Help to preserve mass transport in thriving area

indicators.note: preserving something means keeping it safely held, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a boon is a help or blessing
M is the symbol for mass
to tow is to transport by pulling

explanation.surface: Funding to keep mass transit running in a growing district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help' is a noun, a blessing, which keeps the mass symbol and the transport verb safe inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomtown is a place experiencing rapid growth and prosperity, so it is a thriving area.

clue.text: Degenerate dons curse sign of slowing down

indicators.note: dons as a verb means puts on clothing, so one word wears the other inside it

parts.note: a blight is a curse or plague
a rake is a dissolute, degenerate man

explanation.surface: Decadent university lecturers swear, showing signs of age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' looks like an anagram signal but is a noun for a dissolute man, and 'dons' is not lecturers but a verb meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake light comes on at the back of a vehicle to signal that the driver is slowing.

clue.text: Public commotion behind hospital is upsetting

indicators.note: says the word before it comes after the word that follows it in the answer

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
rowing is noisy quarrelling

explanation.surface: A public scene staged behind a hospital is distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reads as distressing, but it is meant literally: knocking over.
explanation.definitionFit: Overthrowing a ruler or an object means toppling it, which is upsetting in the sense of tipping over.

clue.text: Legacy media at the start is not in retreat

indicators.note: says that letter must be absent from the word that follows, so it is taken out

parts.note: a hermitage is a secluded retreat

indicators.note: only the starting letter of the word before it is wanted

parts.note: the start of media

explanation.surface: Legacy media firms at the outset are not backing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' suggests going backwards, but the retreat is a noun; 'at the start' selects the first letter of media.
explanation.definitionFit: A heritage is what is handed down from earlier generations, so it is an inheritance or legacy.

clue.text: A distress call about most dangerous material

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about in the sense of around, so the call wraps round the next word

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal
best as in the most, the greatest

explanation.surface: An emergency call about a hazardous substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' looks like a quantity but stands for the superlative best, which sits within the distress signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once used for insulation, now known to cause lung disease when inhaled.

clue.text: A stickler for hard work, Mrs Keats sits fulminating

indicators.note: someone fulminating is raging wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An imagined Mrs Keats sits fuming about slackers, a demanding boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskmistress is a woman who imposes heavy workloads, a strict overseer insisting on hard labour.

clue.text: Holiday on far side of Moon? It makes a change

parts.note: leave is time off work

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of Moon

explanation.surface: A holiday on the far side of the moon would make a nice change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far side' sounds astronomical but just takes the end letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaven is yeast or a similar agent that transforms dough, and by extension any influence that alters something.

clue.text: Teetotaller entering place for stiff drink

indicators.note: something entering a place goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a bier holds a corpse, slang a stiff
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal

explanation.surface: A non-drinker walks into a bar wanting a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' looks like part of 'stiff drink' but is slang for a dead body. Bitter is a British style of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a hoppy British draught beer, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Missive about variable architectural feature

indicators.note: about in the sense of around: the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: an epistle is a letter
Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A letter written about some changeable feature of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: Y is a standard algebra variable, the usual crossword way of clueing it; an epistyle is the beam over classical columns.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistyle is the architrave, the main beam resting directly on the tops of classical columns.

clue.text: One who fought J. Frazier with extremely combative hostility

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, written M. Ali in the same style as J. Frazier, his great boxing rival

indicators.note: read as at the extremes, so only the two end letters of the next word are used

parts.note: the extreme letters of combative

explanation.surface: A boxer who took on Joe Frazier showed fierce, combative hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial-plus-surname form of J. Frazier hints that the fighter is written the same way: M. Ali.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to do harm to others, a form of active ill will or hostility.

clue.text: Slight speech problem

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an insult or smear
second meaning: running words indistinctly together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective qualifying the problem, but it is a noun meaning an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a disparaging remark against someone and indistinct, run-together pronunciation.

clue.text: Forecasting tax increases, conservatively at first

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: takes only the opening letters of the words just before it

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An economist predicts tax rises, cautiously at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Value added tax is the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatic means prophetic, predicting the future, so it fits forecasting used as an adjective.

clue.text: Four brave guards gad about

indicators.note: guards stand around what they protect, so the first piece sits within the other

parts.note: gallant means brave
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four courageous sentries wander about idly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' looks like a noun for soldiers, but it is a verb: the brave word surrounds the number.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to roam around in search of pleasure, which is the meaning of the phrasal verb gad about.

clue.text: Wind battering ten rowers

indicators.note: battering knocks something out of shape, so the letters are pounded into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gale pounds a crew of ten oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A nor'wester is a strong wind blowing from the north-west, so a type of wind.

clue.text: Quits the day before exhausted nurses

parts.note: an eve is the day before a festival

indicators.note: exhausted as emptied out, so the inside is gone and only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the outer letters of nurses

explanation.surface: Someone resigns the day before, worn-out nurses walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhausted' means emptied: only the outside letters of the word remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means being even with someone, no debt owed on either side, so evens is equivalent.
